about: Where a program keeps its data (data-folder), so a program built on one machine runs on another: nothing of the build machine is written into its code. `cases`: where an SQLite database opens. A database the project keeps beside it (a relative location) is written data:<program>/<file> by the generator; it opens in the program's data folder: the folder CLARITY_DATA names (Clarity's Run names the project's data folder), else the person's folder for application data (Linux $XDG_DATA_HOME or ~/.local/share, macOS ~/Library/Application Support, Windows %APPDATA%) under the program's name, else under its own name where the program runs. CLARITY_DATA moves any SQLite file under its own name. env:, setting: and :memory: are as they say. `folders`: the program's data folder itself, for `program` ("" when the environment names none: where the program runs); a relative folder setting (its default, or a relative folder the person typed) is in it (conformance/settings.json, `folders`). `stores`: the folder of a file store the project file names with a folder (`filestore photos "data/photos"`): a relative one is written data:<program>/<folder's name> by the generator and is in the data folder under its own name, as an SQLite file is; an absolute one is as it is; env:NAME is that environment variable's value, and with the variable unset or empty (`unset`) the place that uses the store says so in Clarity's own words, by the key variableNotSet with the variable's name in its slot {variable}, and the program does not stop.
